cause.note: review desk round 2 — independent Codex reviewer, eight findings above the severity line, all accepted; five of them corrected overclaims introduced by the round-1 fixes

changes.what: Provenance is decoded inside the package from authentication evidence and carries a class: verified (a signature, a fetched record's hash, or a session token the package re-checked) or asserted (the adapter's word). Anything above requester standing decodes only from verified provenance. The guarantee is restated honestly: nothing the package cannot verify itself can mint standing, an authorization, or a revocation.
changes.why: An adapter-built Provenance was a third construction door, and an adapter that supplies both the bytes and the provenance could pass its own cross-check.

changes.what: The comparison domain is fixed once (same type, same schema version; older versions migrate first, and migration is not a conflict); each type names its immutable fields; the principal, grant, intent, directive, evidence, decision, and authorization equality lines are aligned with the convention; NF-67 and NF-68 restated.
changes.why: The global equality rules contradicted their own applications, and schema evolution would have produced false conflicts.

changes.what: Result claims centralization only: one consumption function plus a lint enumerates every place a refusal is handled; holding rule 42 against a lying report is assigned to the recorded Result on the fact spine (part two) and the verification holders (part nine), and said so.
changes.why: A handler can return whatever a caller's reporting path accepts, so the consumption function did not hold the behaviour claimed for it.

changes.what: Conflict gains one resolution doorway (Conflict plus a verified principal's Decision) and a lint; NF-69 moved from compile to lint.
changes.why: A language cannot stop a function from returning a value it was handed; the compile claim repeated the overclaim just corrected for Result.

changes.what: The repository anchor is the host's non-agent review-approval record required by branch rules on protected paths, with the agent performing the merge as rule 82 requires; a merge event is explicitly not the explicit-yes record.
changes.why: The previous wording required a merge by a non-agent account, contradicting approved rule 82.

changes.what: Fixture citations completed: NF-30 marked Value, NF-40 and NF-42 cite 82 and 98.
changes.why: Three citations survived the round-1 cleanup.

changes.what: Open question 2 now asks about the repository anchor and the initial protected paths instead of the withdrawn decoder-on-the-list idea; open question 3 restated for the new Result shape.
changes.why: The question asked approval of an answer the body no longer gives.

changes.what: Result is two-armed as the approved big picture fixes it; a budget applied as designed is a required capacity field on Success rather than a third arm. Fixture NF-15, the inventory, the tables, and the terms follow.
changes.why: A part design may not silently change a shape its approved parent fixes.

changes.what: Three fixtures added (NF-71 to NF-73) for Provenance construction, class, and evidence verification.
changes.why: The new Provenance decoder needs its own negative contract.

cause.note: review desk round 1 — independent Codex reviewer, seven findings above the severity line, all accepted

changes.what: Authority-bearing values (principal, grant, revocation, authorization) now carry a Provenance established from the authenticated record outside the bytes; their decoders take it as a required input and cross-check every identity-bearing field against it. Authorization gains a required explicit-yes record; a grant's grantor carries its source reference.
changes.why: A faulty adapter could promote content-supplied fields while satisfying every listed shape; nothing bound the value to the record that produced it.

changes.what: Result and Outcome now claim only recognition at compile time; behaviour (a refusal reported as success, a budget applied treated as an error, an uncertain outcome retried) is held by one consumption function plus an architecture lint. Fixtures NF-14, NF-15, NF-46 moved from compile to lint.
changes.why: A tagged union cannot stop a caller from matching a variant and then misbehaving; the guarantee was overstated.

changes.what: The protected-artifact answer is narrowed to repository merges, where the host's branch rules are the external anchor; dashboard-governed and runtime artifacts are declared an open question carried to parts nine and eleven, and the circular 'decoder on its own protected list' claim is removed.
changes.why: Branch protection does not protect artifacts the agent can edit with filesystem authority, and a decoder cannot enforce the list that protects it.

changes.what: Equality is declared three ways (identity, version, value) and each type section names which it supports; same identity with incompatible immutable fields yields a Conflict value, never equality or silent latest-wins.
changes.why: No type actually declared its equality, and identity equality hid the cross-machine conflicts the big picture requires to be recorded.

changes.what: Seventeen negative fixtures added (NF-54 to NF-70) so every named rejection has a stable fixture, and the coverage claim is restated as a build step mapping table cells to fixtures.
changes.why: The claim that every table row was a numbered fixture was false.

changes.what: Rule citations corrected: 100 removed from canonical bytes and authorization; 64 and 75 removed from measurement; 107 and 111 removed from evidence (the weakest-strength aggregate is now a marked Value); 101 and 103 removed from the authorization and requester-authorizer rules; 93 removed from standing grants.
changes.why: Each cited a rule that does not govern the claim.

changes.what: An explicit inventory table lists every constitutional value (eleven core, seven supporting, including Revocation, Provenance, Conflict, UnresolvedInput) with its constructor, and the completeness checks range over it.
changes.why: The prose count of nine types was not stable, so complete schema registration and fixture coverage were uncheckable.
